newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling rises against dollar on exporters.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling rises against dollar on exporters.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened against the dollar on Wednesday in a calm market amid increased exporter sales without corresponding increase in demand, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.03 against the dollar from 56.12 on Tuesday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at an average of 87.71 from 87.91 on Tuesday.
A banker said there was very little interbank activity.
"The market remained quiet with modest inflows of dollars," a dealer said. "Trade opened at 56.00/15 and soon dipped to 55.90/05."

"The central bank came into the market at the close of the day on Tuesday to mop up excess dollars. The central bank is seen as the main reason the shilling has not fully breached the 55 mark," she said.
Dealer said overnight money market rates slid down to between 15 and 20 percent levels.
